# @workerstack/infra

Cloudflare infrastructure as code for workerstack repos

## @workerstack/infra

```sh
bun add -d @workerstack/infra
```

## Config

An `infra.config.ts` describes one product's infrastructure. It default-exports the result of `defineInfraConfig`, which checks the input and fills in defaults.

```ts
import { defineInfraConfig } from "@workerstack/infra";
import { defineEnv } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

// Normally its own file (`web.env.ts`) that the config imports; the account credentials live in its `global` block.
const env = defineEnv({
  dev: {},
  global: { CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210" },
  local: {},
  prod: {},
});

export default defineInfraConfig({
  env,
  cloudflare: {
    zone: { domain: "example.com", zoneId: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" },
  },
  local: {
    host: "example.localhost",
    vars: (origin) => ({ APP_URL: origin.href }),
  },
});
```

`env` is any object with `global`, `local`, `dev` and `prod` views of string values, such as a `defineEnv` instance. `defineInfraConfig` keeps it as given and never reads a value; a command reads the credentials (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) when it runs. A secret field in the config is a type error.

### Products

A product is one `infra.config.ts`. Its name is its directory relative to the repo root, or `.` at the root.

`discoverProducts` finds every config under a root. `selectProducts` picks from them by target.

```ts
import { discoverProducts, selectProducts } from "@workerstack/infra";

const root = process.cwd();
const products = await discoverProducts(root);

selectProducts(root, products, undefined); // the only product, else an error
selectProducts(root, products, { all: true }); // every product
selectProducts(root, products, { name: "apps/web" }); // one product by name
```

The result is `{ ok: true, products }` or `{ ok: false, error }`.

## Credentials

Account credentials live in the product's env file, not in `infra.config.ts`. The config passes the env object. A command reads the credentials only when it runs.

```ts
// apps/web/web.env.ts
import { defineEnv, sealed } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

export const env = defineEnv({
  dev: {},
  global: {
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL: "ops@example.com",
    CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY: sealed("…"),
    CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: sealed("…"),
  },
  local: {},
  prod: {},
});
```

```ts
// apps/web/infra.config.ts
import { defineInfraConfig } from "@workerstack/infra";
import { defineEnv } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

// Normally imported from `./web.env.ts`.
const env = defineEnv({ dev: {}, global: { CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210" }, local: {}, prod: {} });

export default defineInfraConfig({
  env,
  cloudflare: { zone: { domain: "example.com", zoneId: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" } },
});
```

Write a sealed value with `bun repo env set CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY --scope global`. The `env` field is typed `InfraEnv`: any object with `global`, `local`, `dev` and `prod` views of string values (`InfraScope` names the last three). A key read per scope, such as an Access secret, is missing when its view has no value: `ACCESS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET has no prod value; run bun repo env set ACCESS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET --scope prod`.

### Keys

| Key                        | Needed by                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`    | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY`       | `infra run`, `infra cf`   |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`     | `infra cf`                |

An empty string counts as missing.

### Commands

`infra run <dir> <command> [args...]` finds the product that holds `<dir>`. It runs the command with the wrangler credentials of that product. A token from your shell never leaks in.

`infra cf [args...]` finds the product that holds the current directory. It runs `cf` with that product's credentials. It returns the exit code of the child.

`cf` is a peer package. Install it with `bun add -d cf`.

### Errors

A missing key prints one line:

```console
infra run: CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY has no global value; run bun repo env set CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY --scope global
```

### Test runners

Both commands refuse to run when `VITEST` is set or `NODE_ENV` is `test`. The guard runs before any value is read, so a test never decrypts a secret. A test uses a fake instead.

## API client

`createClient(auth, zoneId)` returns a `CfClient`: one `request(method, path, body)` call that parses Cloudflare's response envelope and returns its `result`. A failed envelope throws one line.

```console
CF API GET /zones/abc/dns_records: Invalid zone identifier
```

### accountAuth and CfAuth

`accountAuth(env)` reads the account credentials from `env.global` when it is called. It returns a `CfAuth`: the API token when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is set, else the account email with its global key. A missing key throws the fix line from [credentials](#credentials).

```ts
import { accountAuth, createClient } from "@workerstack/infra";
import type { CfAuth, CfClient } from "@workerstack/infra";

const env = {
  dev: {},
  global: {
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL: "ops@example.com",
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210",
    CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY: "example-key",
  },
  local: {},
  prod: {},
};

const auth: CfAuth = accountAuth(env);
const client: CfClient = createClient(auth, "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef");

export const records = client.request<object[]>("GET", `/zones/${client.zoneId}/dns_records`);
```

### InfraScope

`InfraScope` is `"local" | "dev" | "prod"`. A per-scope secret is read from the env view of that name.

```ts
import type { InfraScope } from "@workerstack/infra";

export const scopes: InfraScope[] = ["local", "dev", "prod"];
```

### SecretWrite and ConfigEdit

Provisioning returns two kinds of change. A `ConfigEdit` is a text edit to a config file, for an id only: a D1 `database_id`, a KV `id`, a Turnstile `siteKey` or an Access `clientId`. A `SecretWrite` is a secret to put in the env under `key` for `scope`, such as `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` or `ACCESS_SERVICE_TOKEN_CLIENT_SECRET`. A secret is never part of an edit.

```ts
import type { ConfigEdit, SecretWrite } from "@workerstack/infra";

export const edit: ConfigEdit = { pattern: 'siteKey: "STUB",', replacement: 'siteKey: "0x4AAAAAAAexample",' };
export const secret: SecretWrite = { key: "TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY", scope: "prod", value: "example-secret" };
```

Write each secret with `bun repo env set <key> --scope <scope>`.

## Commands

Four commands check and change what a product's config describes. Each takes `[name|--all]`.

```console
$ infra get              # the product holding the current dir, else the only product
$ infra get web          # by product name (its dir)
$ infra get --all
$ infra set web
$ infra zone-get web
$ infra zone-set web
```

| Command         | What it does                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `infra get`     | Reports the live Cloudflare account and zone, then Google, Apple and Microsoft, against the config. Changes nothing. |
| `infra set`     | Provisions bindings, Access and AI Search, applies the zone, then applies Google, Apple and Microsoft.            |
| `infra zone-get`| Reports the zone: rules, drift, declared bindings, R2, AI Search and Turnstile.                                   |
| `infra zone-set`| Applies the zone settings only. Zone redirects are not applied yet.                                               |

### Target

- A name picks the product whose directory has that name, as `infra.config.ts` discovery names it.
- `--all` runs every product.
- With no name, the product holding the current directory runs. Outside every product the only product runs; with two or more, the command stops:

```console
infra get: 2 products; name one or pass --all: apps/admin, apps/web
```

An extra argument or an unknown flag prints `usage: infra get [name|--all]` and exits 2.

A failing product prints `infra <command>: <product>: <message>`. The rest still run, and the exit code is 1.

```console
infra zone-get: apps/web: no cloudflare zone in the config
```

### Secret flow

`infra set` writes ids and secrets to different places.

- A new id (a D1 database, a KV namespace, a Microsoft client id) is written into `infra.config.ts` by one file write.
- A new secret never touches the config. The Turnstile secret key, the Access service token secret and a new Microsoft client secret go to `bun repo env set KEY --scope S --file F`, with the value on stdin. `F` is the env file under the product that calls `defineEnv(` and exports the config's `env`.

Each secret prints one line:

```console
wrote TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (prod) with bun repo env set
```

A product with no such env file stops with `no env file under apps/web exports the config's env; define it with defineEnv beside infra.config.ts`.

Microsoft adds a client secret only when the scope has no `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`. A scope that has one gets none, so a rerun adds nothing.

Ids and secrets found before a step fails are still written.

### Keys

`infra get` and `infra set` read `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and the account credentials from `env.global`. They read `APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY` and `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` per scope, and `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PRIVATE_KEY` and `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_API_TOKEN` from `global`. A missing key prints its fix line:

```console
infra set: apps/web: APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY has no prod value; run bun repo env set APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY --scope prod
```

### Test runners

The commands refuse to run under `VITEST` or `NODE_ENV=test`, before any value is read.
